top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P002) stays first on the common criteria. His voice is distinctive: body, childhood memory, dream and metaphysical speculation form one imaginative substance in dense, patterned prose. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid show formal ambition at very large scale and vary in register while keeping one identity. The career has run over several decades from a poetic beginning, which bears on maturity. The citation should centre the novels, with the poetry as ground, since coverage of the poetry in translation is thin. Can Xue (P001) is a close and serious second. Her formal discipline, compression and single narrative method are real strengths, and the compression means repetition costs her less than it would in very long cycles. Round 2 did not show whether her later novels deepen or restate the method, or whether Cărtărescu's later volumes thin, so I do not let the 4-2 split on the slate decide the order. Both judgments rest on public knowledge and translation, not verified reading of the originals, and the order could reasonably go the other way. No award (P000) ranks last, because both proposals name a writer whose oeuvre meets the criteria within the framework of Nobel's will.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. It records no personal or professional tie to Cărtărescu, Can Xue or any other shortlisted writer. My own dream-logic novel Den svarta månens år is context only, a proximity of practice and not evidence of preference. My ties to committee colleagues, including joining the committee with Swärd, are also context only. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
